source_quotes: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;
Both of the applicant’s eyes should also be visible and open in the photograph (see the exception for infants in 8 FAM 402.1-1).
invariants.rationale: Claim P000 captures closure as permission but omits an explicit exception typing or relation connecting it to the open-eyes baseline in P025, and newborn emphasis is not preserved in structured logic.

source_quotes: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;
negative_controls.rationale: The draft confines the rule to infants within scope_text and does not generalize permission to all adults or fabricate resolved targets.

cases.uncertainty: Scope relation between infant closure and general facial expression requirements is unresolved across distant sections.

source_quotes: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.
Head tilt is acceptable for infants;
A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.
invariants.rationale: Discreet support, head tilt permission, and parent face prohibition are each captured independently as discrete claims with correct modalities.

source_quotes: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.
Head tilt is acceptable for infants;
A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft treats car seats as illustrative examples without mandating them, avoids inventing angle constraints, and strictly prohibits parent faces.

source_quotes: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).
A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

Be aware that even if the certificate itself was recently issued, because of U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services processing times, the photograph may not have been taken within six months of submitting the application.
invariants.rationale: The certificate timing caution note is omitted entirely from the draft claims, and the must-request requirement in P004 is not explicitly linked to the six-month standard.

source_quotes: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).
negative_controls.rationale: The draft retains six months without day conversions, preserves likeness and identification predicates, and gives no blanket reuse permission.

cases.uncertainty: The draft completely omitted the certificate timing note from claim extraction.

source_quotes: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;
For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.
invariants.rationale: The draft accurately distinguishes the applicant's lack of signing obligation from the acceptance agent's duty to sign the back for hand-carry applications.

source_quotes: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;
For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft creates no applicant signing duty, does not ban all signatures, and restricts agent signing exclusively to hand-carry cases.

source_quotes: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);
Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).
Immaterial damage is acceptable;
invariants.rationale: In claim P010, the draft conjoins the immaterial categories with AND, erroneously requiring both background damage and non-material facial damage simultaneously.

source_quotes: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).
negative_controls.rationale: Claim P010 defectively formulates choice_text as damage to background AND non-material damage to facial area, committing the conjunction error flagged by the control.

cases.uncertainty: P010 choice_text exhibits conjunctive logic syntax despite the source presenting distinct immaterial categories.

source_quotes: A limited-validity passport using endorsement 46 should be issued when the medical circumstance that requires eyeglasses is temporary and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.
invariants.rationale: P021 preserves the recommendation modality should, endorsement 46, and the dual conditions of temporary medical circumstance and urgent or emergency travel.

source_quotes: A limited-validity passport using endorsement 46 should be issued when the medical circumstance that requires eyeglasses is temporary and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft does not import an unauthorized one-year validity duration, omit endorsement 46, escalate should to must, or drop the temporary medical need condition.

source_quotes: A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances.
Both of the applicant’s eyes should also be visible and open in the photograph (see the exception for infants in 8 FAM 402.1-1).

In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.

Processing and communications/customer service personnel at passport agencies/centers or consular section personnel should refer applications without photographs to their supervisor for guidance on processing passport applications received without photographs;
invariants.rationale: The draft maintains the distinction between the mandatory medical-glasses statement request (must in P016) and advisory should statements in P025, P027, and P028.

source_quotes: In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft does not escalate should recommendations into mandatory duties across the board.

cases.uncertainty: Modality is preserved via issues flags rather than a dedicated advisory taxonomy.

source_quotes: Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-11 received without a photograph from an acceptance facility.
The applicant must re-execute the form DS-11 (see IRL 975-04);
invariants.rationale: Claim P031 incorporates the receipt without photograph from an acceptance facility condition directly in its scope while keeping distinct specialist and applicant actors.

source_quotes: The applicant must re-execute the form DS-11 (see IRL 975-04);
negative_controls.rationale: The re-execution duty in P031 is explicitly scoped to missing photos from acceptance facilities and is not applied to complete DS-11 applications.

source_quotes: Eyeglasses are not acceptable unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons, e.g., the applicant has recently had ocular surgery and the eyeglasses are necessary to protect the applicant’s eyes.
Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.
invariants.rationale: Claims P017 through P020 possess relation none and empty target_ids, lacking structural child links subordinate to the medical glasses acceptance prerequisite.

source_quotes: Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft invents no targets, retains disjunctive groupings in P019 and P020, and conditions tinted lenses strictly on medical statement necessity.

cases.uncertainty: The draft relies on text-based scoping instead of explicit structural parent-child links.

source_quotes: Applicants with physical or mental disabilities, including loss of muscle control (e.g., age-related degeneration or because of a medical condition such as Bell's Palsy), may not be able to produce a natural or unexaggerated expression.
You may accept a photograph without a natural or unexaggerated expression in these circumstances.
invariants.rationale: Claim P024 includes disability circumstances in its scope but sets relation to none and target_ids to empty, omitting structural connection to baseline expression claims P022 and P023.

source_quotes: You may accept a photograph without a natural or unexaggerated expression in these circumstances.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft does not broaden the exception to all disabilities unconditionally and invents no mandatory diagnostic proof.

cases.uncertainty: The baseline-to-exception relationship is conveyed through textual context rather than relational claim identifiers.

source_quotes: If the applicant is unable to open one or both eyes because of a medical condition, you may accept the photograph.

In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.
invariants.rationale: P026 preserves one OR both eyes with causal condition and discretionary acceptance, while P027 correctly models the distinct rare and unlikely trigger for statement requests.

source_quotes: If the applicant is unable to open one or both eyes because of a medical condition, you may accept the photograph.

In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft preserves unlikely without flipping, retains rare cases, and keeps acceptance discretionary under may.

source_quotes: Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.
invariants.rationale: P014 designates the passport application as the returned object, contextualizes printing defects, and keeps requesting a photograph as an uncommanded purpose.

source_quotes: Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft does not make the photograph the returned object or infer an independent must-request command.

source_quotes: See 8 FAM 1001.2 regarding importing photographs for forms DS-5504;
Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-82 or form DS-5504 received without a photograph (see IRL 1000-05 and IRL 1018-14).
invariants.rationale: P029 maintains the unresolved reference to 8 FAM 1001.2 regarding DS-5504 photo importing, and P032 preserves the distinct DS-5504 suspension requirement.

source_quotes: See 8 FAM 1001.2 regarding importing photographs for forms DS-5504;
negative_controls.rationale: The draft invents no remote import procedures and provides no authorization to accept missing-photo DS-5504 forms at the counter.

source_quotes: You must not accept a form DS-11 or form DS-82 received without a photograph at the public counter.
Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-11 received without a photograph from an acceptance facility.
Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-82 or form DS-5504 received without a photograph (see IRL 1000-05 and IRL 1018-14).
invariants.rationale: The draft captures counter refusal for DS-11 OR DS-82, acceptance facility suspension for DS-11, and suspension of DS-82 OR DS-5504 with both IRL references.

source_quotes: You must not accept a form DS-11 or form DS-82 received without a photograph at the public counter.
Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-82 or form DS-5504 received without a photograph (see IRL 1000-05 and IRL 1018-14).
negative_controls.rationale: The draft uses disjunctive grouping without conjunctive distortion and preserves both IRL references.

source_quotes: The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:
Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.
A photograph that appears acceptable and undamaged in the system may have a defect that is apparent when the passport is printed.
invariants.rationale: Reasonableness and potential defect language are kept non-mandatory, but the certificate note was omitted from the claims, making evidence of certificate guidance handling unavailable.

source_quotes: The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:
Applicants may wish to re-use a passport photograph that is depicted on their submitted U.S Certificate of Citizenship or Certificate of Naturalization.
negative_controls.rationale: The draft generates no duties from section titles, revision markers, illustrative examples, or advisory preferences.
